title: Can you get a table at eight?
subtitle: One question tells you more about a ship's dining than any menu it prints.

text: Scarcity onboard is designed. It is not a fact of the sea.
sub: A booking window that opens at midnight ninety days out isn't hospitality under pressure. It is a room built too small for the ship on purpose, and then rationed.

quote: A reservation system is a ship telling you, politely, that it sold more beds than it built chairs.

kicker: What to ask before you book
title: Three questions about the tables

items.head: How many seats, how many beds?
items.body: If the main room cannot seat everyone at a civil hour, someone is eating at half past nine. It may be you.

items.head: Is every restaurant in the fare?
items.body: Where the good rooms carry a cover charge, dinner becomes a nightly purchase decision. That is not restful.

items.head: Open seating or assigned?
items.body: Assigned tables suit some travellers. Being handed one you didn't choose, on a ship that sells freedom, does not.

text: Choose the ship where dinner is a decision at 7.45.
sub: Fewer restaurants, enough seats, no cover charges, no midnight booking scramble. Everything else about the food follows from that, and none of it needs announcing.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Then tell me which sailing you're weighing and I'll tell you honestly whether its dining rooms are big enough for it.
